study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative trajectories of R 1 , R 2 *, and magnetic susceptibility in basal ganglia on healthy ageing

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to compute normative trajectories as a function of age. Prior to GPR, a General Linear Model (GLM) was used to correct for sex and hemispheric effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Utilising the non- parametric Gaussian Process Regression model to derive the normative trajectories... In the following normative modelling analysis, the data were corrected for the sex- specific and inter- hemispherical effects based on the GLM results. Gaussian Process Regression (GRP) ... was used to compute the normative trajectory

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility (χ) in basal ganglia structures. It also modeled normalised tissue volumes of these subcortical ROIs.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we established the normative trajectories of R 1 , R 2 *, and magnetic susceptibility in the basal ganglia at 3T... The tissue volumes of all subcortical ROIs were also extracted and normalised by the intracranial brain volume.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Chan2025B.pdf.md: Abstract / Paragraph 1; 2.2.3. Metrics of interest / Paragraph 2

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models used Age as the primary predictor in GPR. Sex and Hemisphere were used as covariates in a GLM correction step. Age^2 was also included in the GLM.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Gaussian Process Regression (GRP) ... was used to compute the normative trajectory of the sex- and hemispheric- corrected qMRI metrics as a function of age... The design matrix comprised four regressors: Age, Age 2 , Sex, and (left- / right- ) Hemisphere
